acquirer: Funds advised by Apax Partners LLP
target: Finastra Treasury and Capital Markets (TCM) division (subsequently spun out as 'Teciem')

deal_value.notes: Financial terms not officially disclosed; ~$2B including debt was reported by press citing Reuters/sources familiar with the negotiations — treat as an unofficial estimate

calculable.calculation: ~$2,000M reported deal value (incl. debt) / ~$200M reported TCM EBITDA = ~10x
inputs: ~$2B deal value including debt (unofficial, press-reported) — Fintech Futures citing Reuters, https://www.fintechfutures.com/m-a/apax-affiliate-to-acquire-finastras-treasury-and-capital-markets-business

TCM business generates about $200M EBITDA — Octus (formerly Reorg) reporting on the sale process and bank financing, https://octus.com/resources/articles/apax-close-to-acquiring-finastra-treasury-cap-markets-units/
calculable.caveats: Both inputs are unofficial: deal value is a sourced press estimate (terms never disclosed by the parties) and the ~$200M EBITDA is from debt-market reporting, with period/definition unclear. No standalone TCM revenue figure found, so no revenue multiple computable.

sources.title: Finastra to Sell Treasury and Capital Markets Division to Apax Funds (PR Newswire, May 2025)
Apax affiliate to acquire Finastra's Treasury and Capital Markets business (Fintech Futures)
Apax Close to Acquiring Finastra Treasury and Cap Markets Unit, Lines Up Bank Financing (Octus)
Apax spins out Finastra treasury and capital markets business as Teciem (Finextra)

notes: Confirmed this is the TCM carve-out announced May 2025 (agreement signed; sale by Vista Equity Partners-owned Finastra to an Apax affiliate; Evercore sell-side advisor; expected close H1 2026; unit rebranded Teciem) — not any other Apax/Finastra transaction. No multiple published anywhere credible; the ~10x EV/EBITDA is indicative only, built entirely on unofficial reported figures.
